	displayOptions = self.params.values.displayOptions
	metrics = {'targetCount': 0, 'infeedCount': 0, 'outfeedCount': 0, 'wasteCount': 0, 'infeedUnits': '', 'outfeedUnits': '', 'wasteUnits': '', 'targetRate': '', 'actualRate': '', 'rateUnits': 'hr', 'runtimeSecs': 0, 'packageCounts': ''}
	infeedUnits = []
	outfeedUnits = []
	wasteUnits = []
	packageCount = []

	if value['data'] is None:
		self.custom.metrics = metrics
		return {}
		
	self.custom.info = {"showBar": True, "text": "Building chart data...", "type": "INFO"}			
	
	infeed = {}
	outfeed = {}
	waste = {}
	target = {}

	for row in value['data']:
		if row['infeedUnits']: infeedUnits.append(row['infeedUnits'])
		infeedCount = row['infeedCount'] or 0.0
		infeed[row['hourTimeStamp']] = infeed[row['hourTimeStamp']] + infeedCount if infeed.has_key(row['hourTimeStamp']) else infeedCount
		metrics['infeedCount'] += infeedCount
		
		if row['outfeedUnits']: outfeedUnits.append(row['outfeedUnits'])
		outfeedCount = row['outfeedCount'] or 0.0
		outfeed[row['hourTimeStamp']] = outfeed[row['hourTimeStamp']] + outfeedCount if outfeed.has_key(row['hourTimeStamp']) else outfeedCount
		metrics['outfeedCount'] += outfeedCount

		if row['wasteUnits']: wasteUnits.append(row['wasteUnits'])
		wasteCount = row['wasteCount'] or 0.0
		waste[row['hourTimeStamp']] = waste[row['hourTimeStamp']] + wasteCount if waste.has_key(row['hourTimeStamp']) else wasteCount
		metrics['wasteCount'] += wasteCount
		
		targetCount = row['targetCount'] or 0.0
		target[row['hourTimeStamp']] = target[row['hourTimeStamp']] + targetCount if target.has_key(row['hourTimeStamp']) else targetCount
		metrics['targetCount'] += targetCount
		
		packageCount.append(row['packageCount'] or 1)
		
		metrics['runtimeSecs'] += row['runtimeSecs'] or 0

	# A series with nothing counted in the range isn't plotted (its card is hidden too)
	data = {}
	if displayOptions.showInfeed and metrics['infeedCount']: data['infeed'] = [{"category": count[0], "value": count[1]} for count in sorted(infeed.items())]
	if displayOptions.showOutfeed and metrics['outfeedCount']: data['outfeed'] = [{"category": count[0], "value": count[1]} for count in sorted(outfeed.items())]
	if displayOptions.showWaste and metrics['wasteCount']: data['waste'] = [{"category": count[0], "value": count[1]} for count in sorted(waste.items())]
	if displayOptions.showTarget and metrics['targetCount']: data['target'] = [{"category": count[0], "value": count[1]} for count in sorted(target.items())]
	
	infeedUnits = list(set(infeedUnits)) if len(infeedUnits) > 0 else ['']
	metrics['infeedUnits'] = infeedUnits[0] if len(infeedUnits) == 1 else 'mixed'
	
	outfeedUnits = list(set(outfeedUnits)) if len(outfeedUnits) > 0 else ['']
	metrics['outfeedUnits'] = outfeedUnits[0] if len(outfeedUnits) == 1 else 'mixed'
	
	wasteUnits = list(set(wasteUnits)) if len(wasteUnits) > 0 else ['']
	metrics['wasteUnits'] = wasteUnits[0] if len(wasteUnits) == 1 else 'mixed'
	
	packageCounts = list(set(packageCount)) if len(packageCount) > 0 else ['']
	metrics['packageCounts'] = packageCounts[0] if len(packageCounts) == 1 else 'mixed'
	
	metrics['targetRate'] = metrics['targetCount'] / (metrics['runtimeSecs'] / 3600.0) if metrics['targetCount'] > 0 and  metrics['runtimeSecs'] > 0 else 0
	metrics['actualRate'] = metrics['infeedCount'] / (metrics['runtimeSecs'] / 3600.0) if metrics['infeedCount'] > 0 and  metrics['runtimeSecs'] > 0 else 0
	
	self.custom.metrics = metrics
	
	self.custom.info = {"showBar": False, "text": "", "type": "INFO"}		

	return data

# Slow cycles (868mwz9ey): a diamond for each unit the open run should make, at the time it's due (the run's start + n / the
	# standard rate, however long it was down) and at its count. Only while the range reaches now, for an open Production run
	# with a standard rate, the target shown (showTarget) and a cycle at least displayOptions.dueMarkerMinCycleMins long (5
	# when not set); the diamonds then replace the target line (custom.plots). The count is the plotted line: outfeed, or
	# infeed when there's no outfeed (or it's in other units than the target), counted from where it stood at the run's
	# start (or the range's, when the run started before it; the units due before that aren't shown)
	import math
	values = value['values'] or {}
	opts = values.get('displayOptions') or {}
	start, end, assetId = values.get('startDate'), values.get('endDate'), values.get('assetId')
	if assetId is None or start is None or end is None or not opts.get('showTarget'): return None
	now = system.date.toMillis(system.date.now())
	t0, t1 = system.date.toMillis(start), system.date.toMillis(end)
	# Current Run's end is moved to now every minute, so a range up to two minutes old still reaches now
	if t1 < now - 120000: return None
	run = None
	for r in value['runs'] or []:
		if r.get('open'): run = r
	if run is None or not run['production'] or not run['standardRate'] or run['standardRate'] <= 0: return None
	try:
		mins = float(opts.get('dueMarkerMinCycleMins')) if opts.get('dueMarkerMinCycleMins') is not None else 5.0
	except:
		mins = 5.0
	secsPer = {'second': 1, 'minute': 60, 'hour': 3600, 'day': 86400, 'week': 604800}.get((run['period'] or 'hour').lower(), 3600)
	cycle = secsPer * 1000.0 / run['standardRate']
	if cycle < mins * 60000: return None
	runStart = run.get('start') or run['x']
	first = max(runStart, t0)
	metrics = value['metrics'] or {}
	lines = dict([(s['name'], s['data']) for s in value['series'] or []])
	same = not metrics.get('infeedUnits') or (metrics.get('outfeedUnits') or '') == metrics.get('infeedUnits')
	track = 'Outfeed' if 'Outfeed' in lines and same else 'Infeed' if 'Infeed' in lines else 'Outfeed' if 'Outfeed' in lines else None
	data = [[p[0], p[1]] for p in (lines.get(track) or [])]
	def at(t):
		# The line's value at t: straight between its points, held through a gap; 0 before it starts
		v, prev = 0.0, None
		for x, y in data:
			if y is None: continue
			if x >= t:
				if x == t: return y
				if prev is None: return v
				return prev[1] + (y - prev[1]) * float(t - prev[0]) / (x - prev[0])
			prev, v = (x, y), y
		return v
	base = at(first)
	latest = [y for x, y in data if y is not None]
	reached = max(int(math.floor((latest[-1] if latest else base) - base + 0.05)), 0)
	def crossing(y):
		# When the line first got to y (between two of its points)
		px, py = first, base
		for x, v in data:
			if v is None or x <= first: continue
			if v >= y - 0.05:
				return x if v <= py else max(px, px + (y - py) * float(x - px) / (v - py))
			px, py = x, v
		return None
	# The units due before the line's start, and the next one due (after now, not made yet): the last one shown, so the count
	# axis isn't stretched to the end of a range that runs on past now (Today)
	n0 = int(math.floor((first - runStart) / cycle + 1e-9))
	nNext = max(n0 + reached + 1, int(math.floor((now - runStart) / cycle)) + 1)
	# Hundreds of diamonds would be noise: the target line stays instead
	if nNext - n0 > 400: return None
	# When each count came: the line spreads an hour's counts over the hour, so a count's own time is only known while the
	# chart is open. custom.dueSeen keeps the time a refresh (every minute) first saw the total go up, per run; an earlier count
	# is read off the line
	seen = {}
	col = {'Infeed': 1, 'Outfeed': 2}.get(track)
	ld = value['lines'] or {}
	if col is not None and str(ld.get('key') or '').startswith('%s|%s|%s|' % (assetId, t0, t1)):
		total = sum([r[col] or 0 for r in ld.get('rows') or []])
		key = '%s|%s|%s|%s' % (assetId, runStart, t0, track)
		prev = self.custom.dueSeen or {}
		known = prev.get('key') == key
		arrivals = [[a[0], a[1]] for a in (prev.get('arrivals') or [])] if known else []
		if known and prev.get('at') is not None and now - prev['at'] <= 180000 and 0 < total - (prev.get('sum') or 0) <= 5:
			arrivals.append([now, total - prev['sum']])
		arrivals = arrivals[-200:]
		self.custom.dueSeen = {'key': key, 'at': now, 'sum': total, 'arrivals': arrivals}
		# The newest counts are the top units
		u = reached
		for a in reversed(arrivals):
			for k in range(int(a[1])):
				if u >= 1 and a[0] >= first: seen[u] = a[0]
				u -= 1
	# Times in the device's time zone, as the plot shows them: the time alone today, else with the date
	from java.text import SimpleDateFormat
	from java.util import TimeZone
	def dfmt(ms, pattern):
		f = SimpleDateFormat(pattern)
		if value['tz']: f.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone(value['tz']))
		return f.format(system.date.fromMillis(long(ms)))
	today = dfmt(now, 'yyyyMMdd')
	dated = system.kanoa.date.localizeDateFormat('MMM d, HH:mm', self.session.props.locale)
	hm = lambda ms: dfmt(ms, 'HH:mm') if dfmt(ms, 'yyyyMMdd') == today else dfmt(ms, dated)
	# A count not seen arriving came some time in the interval (hour, or day) where the line reached it, up to now
	hours = ld.get('hours') or 1
	starts = sorted([r[0] for r in ld.get('rows') or []])
	def made(u):
		if u in seen: return seen[u], seen[u]
		c = crossing(base + u) or now
		lo = max([s for s in starts if s < c] or [None])
		if lo is None or c > lo + hours * 3600000: return c, c
		return max(lo, first), min(lo + hours * 3600000, now)
	# met: made by its due time (or in the interval it fell in); late: made after it (stays red); missed: due and not made;
	# upcoming: not due yet
	units = []
	for n in range(n0 + 1, nNext + 1):
		due = runStart + n * cycle
		u = n - n0
		lo, hi = made(u) if u <= reached else (None, None)
		when = None if lo is None else ('at %s' % hm(hi)) if lo == hi else ('between %s and %s' % (hm(lo), hm(hi)))
		if lo is not None and lo <= due: state, text = 'met', ('met at %s' % hm(hi)) if lo == hi else 'met, made %s' % when
		elif lo is not None: state, text = 'late', 'missed, made %s' % when
		elif due <= now: state, text = 'missed', 'missed'
		else: state, text = 'upcoming', 'not yet'
		units.append({'x': long(due), 'y': round(base + u, 1), 'n': n, 'state': state, 'tip': u'Unit %d due %s \u00b7 %s' % (n, hm(due), text),
			'label': ('%d due %s' % (n, hm(due))) if n == nNext else None})
	# The time axis reaches the next one due, with a little room after it
	nextDue = runStart + nNext * cycle
	reach = nextDue + (nextDue - t0) * 0.03
	return {'track': track, 'units': units, 'ymax': max([u['y'] for u in units]) if units else None, 'xmax': long(reach) if reach > t1 else None}

# What ran in Production, item by item: a run of the same item and work order back to back (other modes between don't
	# break it) is one, with its standard rate (the target's slope) and its production time
	items = []
	for run in value or []:
		if not run['production'] or not run['itemName']: continue
		if items and items[-1]['name'] == run['itemName'] and items[-1]['workOrder'] == run['workOrderName'] and items[-1]['rate'] == run['standardRate']:
			items[-1]['x2'] = run['x2']
			items[-1]['secs'] += (run['x2'] - run['x']) / 1000
			continue
		items.append({'name': run['itemName'], 'workOrder': run['workOrderName'], 'color': run['itemColor'], 'rate': run['standardRate'], 'period': run['period'], 'units': run['units'],
			'x': run['x'], 'x2': run['x2'], 'secs': (run['x2'] - run['x']) / 1000})
	return items

# What the summary's lines link to: the asset (path and name for the popups) and the chart's range, and what the user can act on
	# as the screens they open check it: editOperations on the asset (or one above it) for downtime, speed loss and counts/scrap
	# (the Asset Operation info panel and the downtime table), enterQualityCheck for checks (the check sheet event screens),
	# configureWorkOrders for maintenance (the work order event editor); a gateway admin can do all of them. The rights are read
	# for the logged-in user as those screens read them (getUserAssetCRUD), not from session.custom.kanoa.security, which only
	# the header's login sets (a page without it keeps the default, with no user). If they can't be read, every line links: the
	# screens check the rights themselves
	values = value['values'] or {}
	assetId, start, end = values.get('assetId'), values.get('startDate'), values.get('endDate')
	out = {'assetId': assetId, 'assetPath': None, 'assetName': None, 'start': start, 'end': end,
		'canEditOperations': False, 'canEnterChecks': False, 'canEditWorkOrders': False}
	if assetId is None or start is None or end is None: return out
	assets = system.kanoa.asset.getAssets({'assetId': assetId})
	out['assetPath'] = system.kanoa.utilities.getFieldValue('assetPath', assets)
	out['assetName'] = system.kanoa.utilities.getFieldValue('assetName', assets)
	try:
		userId = system.kanoa.security.getIDPUserId(value['user'])
		crud = system.kanoa.security.getUserAssetCRUD(userId) if userId is not None else None
	except:
		crud = None
	if not isinstance(crud, dict) or not crud:
		system.util.getLogger('kanoa.productionCounts').debug('No rights read for the summary links (user %s): every line links' % (value['user'] or {}).get('userName'))
		out.update({'canEditOperations': True, 'canEnterChecks': True, 'canEditWorkOrders': True})
		return out
	assetPath = out['assetPath'] or ''
	def allowed(right, perAsset):
		entry = crud.get(right) or {}
		if not entry.get('enabled'): return False
		paths = list(entry.get('assets') or [])
		return not perAsset or not paths or any(assetPath == a or assetPath.startswith(a + '\\') for a in paths)
	admin = bool(crud.get('isGatewayAdmin'))
	out['canEditOperations'] = admin or allowed('editOperations', True)
	out['canEnterChecks'] = admin or allowed('enterQualityCheck', False)
	out['canEditWorkOrders'] = admin or allowed('configureWorkOrders', False)
	return out

# The mode periods (displayOptions.showModes; on when it isn't set): runs of the same mode back to back (a new item or work
	# order) are one band
	options = (value['values'] or {}).get('displayOptions') or {}
	if options.get('showModes') is False: return []
	bands = []
	for run in value['runs'] or []:
		if bands and bands[-1]['name'] == run['modeName'] and bands[-1]['x2'] >= run['x']:
			bands[-1]['x2'] = max(bands[-1]['x2'], run['x2'])
			continue
		bands.append({'name': run['modeName'], 'production': run['production'], 'color': run['modeColor'], 'x': run['x'], 'x2': run['x2']})
	return bands

# The series split into plots by units, stacked on a shared time axis: one plot when every series is in the same units,
	# otherwise the first series' units on top and the others' below (a third unit, unlikely, joins the top plot).
	# xmin/xmax keep the plots' time axes the same
	units = dict([(s['name'], '' if s['units'] == 'mixed' else s['units']) for s in (value['units'] or [])])
	plots = []
	for s in value['series'] or []:
		u = units.get(s['name'], '')
		for plot in plots:
			if plot['units'] == u:
				plot['series'].append(s)
				break
		else:
			plots.append({'units': u, 'series': [s]})
	if len(plots) > 2:
		for plot in plots[2:]: plots[0]['series'] += plot['series']
		plots = plots[:2]
	# Slow cycles: the due diamonds (custom.dueUnits) go on the plot with the line they're measured against and replace the
	# target line. A target with nothing else on its plot yet (nothing counted) keeps it, drawn with no line (stroke)
	due = value['due']
	home = None
	if due and due.get('units'):
		for p in plots:
			if due.get('track') and [s for s in p['series'] if s['name'] == due['track']]: home = p
		if home is None:
			for p in plots:
				if [s for s in p['series'] if s['name'] == 'Target']: home = p
		if home is not None:
			for p in plots:
				others = [s for s in p['series'] if s['name'] != 'Target']
				if others or p is not home: p['series'] = others
			plots = [p for p in plots if p['series']]
			home['due'], home['dueMax'] = due['units'], due['ymax']
	# The whole range, to its end: the counts stop at now, and the events plot shows what's scheduled after it
	values = value['values'] or {}
	xs = [p[0] for s in (value['series'] or []) for p in s['data']]
	xmin = system.date.toMillis(values['startDate']) if values.get('startDate') is not None else (min(xs) if xs else None)
	xmax = system.date.toMillis(values['endDate']) if values.get('endDate') is not None else (max(xs) if xs else None)
	# ...and on to the next unit due, when it's after the range's end
	if home is not None and due.get('xmax') and xmax is not None: xmax = max(xmax, due['xmax'])
	# A plot's lines share one set of times, so the tooltip lists every line at the hovered time: ApexCharts draws a shared
	# tooltip only when its series are the same length with the same x at each index, otherwise it shows the nearest series
	# alone. Each line gets a point at every time any line in the plot has one, its value read off its own line there
	# (straight between its points, null in its gaps and outside its own times)
	def aligned(data, xs):
		points = [[p[0], p[1]] for p in data]
		out, i, n = [], 0, len(points)
		for x in xs:
			while i + 1 < n and points[i + 1][0] <= x: i += 1
			if n == 0 or x < points[0][0] or x > points[-1][0]: y = None
			elif points[i][0] == x: y = points[i][1]
			else:
				(xa, ya), (xb, yb) = points[i], points[i + 1]
				y = None if ya is None or yb is None else round(ya + (yb - ya) * float(x - xa) / (xb - xa), 1)
			out.append([x, y])
		return out
	for plot in plots:
		plot['xmin'], plot['xmax'] = xmin, xmax
		if len(plot['series']) > 1:
			xs = sorted(set([p[0] for s in plot['series'] for p in s['data']]))
			plot['series'] = [dict(s, data=aligned(s['data'], xs)) for s in plot['series']]
	return plots

# Each run in Production over the range (up to now), in order: its work order and item, counts, time and rates, over the
	# range's part of the run (strictDates) and with its start and end, which open the Count Editor for it (rptRunCounts). The
	# actual rate is the run's infeed over its run time
	values = value['values'] or {}
	start, end, assetId = values.get('startDate'), values.get('endDate'), values.get('assetId')
	if assetId is None or start is None or end is None: return []
	now = system.date.now()
	upTo = now if system.date.isBefore(now, end) else end
	if not system.date.isAfter(upTo, start): return []
	data = system.kanoa.event.getAssetProductionEvents({'assetId': assetId, 'startDate': start, 'endDate': upTo, 'strictDates': True})
	if data is None or isinstance(data, basestring): return []
	runs = []
	for r in sorted(system.dataset.toPyDataSet(data), key=lambda r: system.date.toMillis(r['startDate'])):
		if r['modeTypeName'] != 'Production' or not r['itemName']: continue
		# The run's part of the range, as its counts are (strictDates): the Count Editor opens for the same time
		runStart = start if system.date.isBefore(r['startDate'], start) else r['startDate']
		runEnd = upTo if r['endDate'] is None or system.date.isAfter(r['endDate'], upTo) else r['endDate']
		run = {'workOrder': r['workOrderName'], 'item': r['itemName'], 'infeedUnits': r['infeedUnits'], 'outfeedUnits': r['outfeedUnits'],
			'wasteUnits': r['wasteUnits'], 'period': r['period'], 'rates': [r['standardRate']] if r['standardRate'] else [],
			'startDate': runStart, 'endDate': runEnd, 'rateTimesSecs': 0.0, 'rateSecs': 0}
		for k in ('durationSecs', 'runtimeSecs', 'targetCount', 'infeedCount', 'outfeedCount', 'wasteCount'): run[k] = r[k] or 0
		# A run that never ran has no actual rate
		if r['runtimeSecs'] and r['durationSecs']:
			run['rateTimesSecs'] = float(r['infeedCount'] or 0) / r['runtimeSecs'] * r['durationSecs']
			run['rateSecs'] = r['durationSecs']
		runs.append(run)
	return runs

# The asset's runs (mode events: a mode with its item and standard rate) over the chart's range, oldest first, clipped to

# Running totals: each line grows by its count every interval, so the gap between outfeed and target is how far behind
	# or ahead the period is. Production of a different item or work order starts the lines from 0 again, so a line shows
	# that run's counts; a break in another mode (cleaning, say) and back to the same item and order carries on counting.
	# A series hidden in the display options isn't in chartData.
	# Counts (and the target) only build up in Production, so an interval's count rises across the Production time inside it
	# and stays flat through the other modes; an interval with no Production run rises across the interval
	data, theme, values = value['data'] or {}, value['theme'], value['values'] or {}
	start, end, interval = values.get('startDate'), values.get('endDate'), values.get('interval')
	def ms(x):
		return system.date.toMillis(x) if hasattr(x, 'getTime') else x
	# The lines use custom.lineData (counts by hour, or by day for a long range), so they rise when the counts came; a series
	# shows when it's in chartData (display options, something counted)
	lines = value['lines'] or {}
	hours = lines.get('hours') or 1
	byKey = {}
	for n, key in enumerate(['infeed', 'outfeed', 'waste', 'target']):
		byKey[key] = [{'category': r[0], 'value': r[n + 1]} for r in lines.get('rows') or [] if r[n + 1]]
	last = min(ms(end), ms(system.date.now())) if end is not None else ms(system.date.now())
	first = ms(start) if start is not None else None
	# Production time, as one span per run: not merged, so no span crosses the start of a run
	production = sorted([[r['x'], r['x2']] for r in value['runs'] or [] if r['production']])
	# Where the lines start from 0: a Production run whose item or work order isn't the previous Production run's
	runStarts, previous = [], None
	for r in sorted(value['runs'] or [], key=lambda r: r['x']):
		if not r['production']: continue
		key = (r['itemName'], r['workOrderName'])
		if previous is not None and key != previous and (first is None or r['x'] > first): runStarts.append(r['x'])
		previous = key
	def restart(t, total, line, resets):
		# Back to 0 at each run that starts by t: the line ends at the old total and breaks (a null point) before it
		while resets and resets[0] <= t:
			r = resets.pop(0)
			# A point at the run's start (an interval ending there) moves just before it, so the break comes after it
			while line and line[-1][0] >= r - 1: line.pop()
			line.append([r - 1, round(total, 1)])
			line.append([r - 0.5, None])
			line.append([r, 0.0])
			total = 0.0
		return total
	def spans(a, b):
		return [[max(a, s), min(b, e)] for s, e in production if min(b, e) > max(a, s)]
	series = []
	for key, name, token in [('infeed', 'Infeed', '--kcPrimary'), ('outfeed', 'Outfeed', '--kcTertiary'),
			('waste', 'Waste', '--kcError'), ('target', 'Target', '--kcOnSurfaceVariant')]:
		if data.get(key) is None: continue
		points = byKey.get(key) or []
		# From 0 at the range's start, so a line with nothing counted yet runs flat (in Production) like the target
		total, line = 0.0, ([[first, 0.0]] if first is not None else [])
		resets = list(runStarts)
		for p in points:
			a = ms(p['category'])
			a = max(a, first) if first is not None else a
			b = min(ms(p['category']) + hours * 3600000, last)
			if b < a: b = a
			count = p['value'] or 0
			total = restart(a, total, line, resets)
			if not line or line[-1][0] < a: line.append([a, round(total, 1)])
			inside = spans(a, b)
			secs = float(sum([e - s for s, e in inside]))
			if secs > 0:
				for s, e in inside:
					total = restart(s, total, line, resets)
					if line[-1][0] < s: line.append([s, round(total, 1)])
					total += count * (e - s) / secs
					line.append([e, round(total, 1)])
				if line[-1][0] < b: line.append([b, round(total, 1)])
			else:
				total += count
				line.append([b, round(total, 1)])
		# Flat from the last interval with counts to now (or the range's end): nothing more was counted, apart from the runs
		# that started since
		total = restart(last, total, line, resets)
		if line and line[-1][0] < last: line.append([last, round(total, 1)])
		# No line outside Production: a gap (a null point) between two points with no Production time between them and no
		# count added across them
		if production:
			gapped = []
			for a, b in zip(line, line[1:] + [None]):
				gapped.append(a)
				if b is not None and b[0] > a[0] and b[1] == a[1] and not spans(a[0], b[0]): gapped.append([(a[0] + b[0]) / 2, None])
			line = gapped
		series.append({'name': name, 'type': 'line', 'color': kanoaScripts.colors.getCSSColor(token, theme), 'data': line})
	return series

# Each series shown and its units, in the chart's series order: infeed and target are in infeed units, waste in waste units
	# and outfeed in outfeed units
	data, metrics = value['data'] or {}, value['metrics'] or {}
	units = {'infeed': metrics.get('infeedUnits'), 'target': metrics.get('infeedUnits'), 'waste': metrics.get('wasteUnits'),

		if data.get(key) is not None]
return True

# The asset's downtime (its downtime state events) and speed loss (performance events: slow running, with a reason and the # minutes lost) over the chart's range, for the timeline plot: each a bar from start to end, clipped to the range and to now, # with a colour and a hover text. Refreshed every minute; the schedule is custom.schedule (every 10 minutes) from cgi import escape values = value['values'] or {} start, end, assetId = values.get('startDate'), values.get('endDate'), values.get('assetId') empty = {'downtime': [], 'performance': []} if assetId is None or start is None or end is None: return empty now = system.date.now() t0, t1, tNow = system.date.toMillis(start), system.date.toMillis(end), system.date.toMillis(now) # Times in the device's time zone, as the plot shows them from java.text import SimpleDateFormat from java.util import TimeZone def dfmt(d, pattern): f = SimpleDateFormat(pattern) if value['tz']: f.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone(value['tz'])) return f.format(d) fmt = lambda d: dfmt(d, 'MMM d, HH:mm') text = lambda secs: system.kanoa.utilities.secondsToText(int(secs), {'showSecs': False, 'showDays': False}) or '' downtime = [] data = system.kanoa.event.getAssetStateEvents({'assetId': assetId, 'startDate': start, 'endDate': end, 'showDowntimeOnly': True}) for e in system.dataset.toPyDataSet(data) if data is not None else []: if e['startDate'] is None: continue s = max(system.date.toMillis(e['startDate']), t0) x2 = min(system.date.toMillis(e['endDate']) if e['endDate'] is not None else tNow, t1, tNow) if x2 <= s: continue lines = ['%s · %s' % (escape(e['stateName'] or ''), escape(e['stateTypeName'] or ''))] if e['stateCategoryName']: lines.append(escape(e['stateCategoryName'])) if e['note']: lines.append(escape(e['note'])) lines.append('%s to %s (%s)' % (fmt(e['startDate']), fmt(e['endDate']) if e['endDate'] is not None else 'now', text((x2 - s) / 1000))) downtime.append({'x': s, 'x2': x2, 'label': e['stateName'], 'type': e['stateTypeName'], 'color': e['stateColor'] or e['stateTypeColor'] or '#ba1a1a', 'secs': (x2 - s) / 1000, 'tip': '
'.join(lines)}) # Performance events: getPerformanceEvents filters on the start, so it reads from a week before the range for one already # going; an active one (endDate now) runs to now performance = [] # Read defensively: a failure here leaves the row empty instead of the whole timeline, and logs why try: data = system.kanoa.event.getPerformanceEvents({'assetId': assetId, 'startDate': system.date.addDays(start, -7), 'endDate': end}) if data is not None and not isinstance(data, basestring): cols = list(data.getColumnNames()) for row in system.dataset.toPyDataSet(data): e = dict(zip(cols, list(row))) if e.get('startDate') is None: continue active = e.get('isActive') or e.get('endDate') is None s = max(system.date.toMillis(e['startDate']), t0) x2 = min(tNow if active else system.date.toMillis(e['endDate']), t1, tNow) if x2 <= s: continue name = e.get('performanceStateName') or 'Unassigned' # autoReason is a flag; an automatic event's note says why (e.g. Below 95% of the standard rate) lines = ['%s%s' % (escape(name), ' · automatic' if e.get('isAuto') else '')] if e.get('note'): lines.append(escape(unicode(e['note']))) lines.append('%s to %s (%s)' % (fmt(e['startDate']), 'now' if active else fmt(e['endDate']), text((x2 - s) / 1000))) # The minutes lost over the whole event; the share inside the range (as the bar is clipped) counts toward the totals lostAll = float(e.get('value') or 0) * 60 full = float((tNow if active else system.date.toMillis(e['endDate'])) - system.date.toMillis(e['startDate'])) lost = lostAll * min(1.0, (x2 - s) / full) if full > 0 else lostAll if lostAll: lines.append('%s lost%s' % (text(lostAll), (' (%s in this range)' % text(lost)) if lostAll - lost >= 60 else '')) performance.append({'x': s, 'x2': x2, 'label': name, 'color': e.get('performanceStateColor') or '#9ca3af', 'lostSecs': lost, 'tip': '
'.join(lines)}) elif data is not None: system.util.getLogger('kanoa.productionCounts').warn('getPerformanceEvents: %s' % data) except: import sys system.util.getLogger('kanoa.productionCounts').warn('Performance events for the timeline failed: %s' % (sys.exc_info()[1],)) downtime.sort(key=lambda b: b['x']) performance.sort(key=lambda b: b['x']) return {'downtime': downtime, 'performance': performance}

# The timeline's rows (custom.timeline) plus Actual and Tooling (custom.tooling, below): a bar per run in every mode, back to back runs with the same mode, item # and work order as one; each in its mode's colour. The hover has the mode, item, work # order and required quantity from cgi import escape out = dict(value['timeline'] or {}) # the schedule comes from custom.schedule (every 10 minutes) out['schedule'] = list(value['schedule'] or []) # Times in the device's time zone, as the plot shows them from java.text import SimpleDateFormat from java.util import TimeZone def dfmt(d, pattern): f = SimpleDateFormat(pattern) if value['tz']: f.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone(value['tz'])) return f.format(d) fmt = lambda x: dfmt(system.date.fromMillis(long(x)), 'MMM d, HH:mm') fallback = kanoaScripts.colors.getCSSColor('--kcPrimary', value['theme']) or '#489fe2' grey = kanoaScripts.colors.getCSSColor('--kcOutline', value['theme']) or '#9ca3af' runs = [] for run in value['runs'] or []: last = runs[-1] if runs else None if last and last['modeName'] == run['modeName'] and last['itemName'] == run['itemName'] and last['workOrderName'] == run['workOrderName'] and last['x2'] >= run['x']: runs[-1] = dict(last, x2=max(last['x2'], run['x2'])) else: runs.append(run) actual = [] for run in runs: lines = ['%s%s' % (escape(run['modeName'] or ''), (' · %s' % escape(run['itemName'])) if run['itemName'] else '')] if run['workOrderName']: lines.append('Work order %s%s' % (escape(run['workOrderName']), (', %s %s required' % ('{:,g}'.format(float(run['reqdQty'])), escape(run['outfeedUnits'] or ''))) if run['reqdQty'] else '')) lines.append('%s to %s (%s)' % (fmt(run['x']), fmt(run['x2']), system.kanoa.utilities.secondsToText(int((run['x2'] - run['x']) / 1000), {'showSecs': False, 'showDays': False}) or '')) #The Actual row shows the run's mode in its mode colour, as the Schedule row does (items have their own lines on the count plots) color = run['modeColor'] or (fallback if run['production'] else grey) actual.append({'x': run['x'], 'x2': run['x2'], 'label': run['modeName'], 'color': color, 'tip': '
'.join(lines)}) #A new Production run with a different item starts after a sliver of the chart's background, so back to back runs read #as separate bars (the bar ends a little early; its hover keeps the run's real times) if runs: gap = (max(r['x2'] for r in runs) - min(r['x'] for r in runs)) * 0.003 for i in range(1, len(runs)): prev, run = runs[i - 1], runs[i] if prev['production'] and run['production'] and prev['itemName'] != run['itemName'] and prev['x2'] >= run['x']: actual[i - 1]['x2'] = max(actual[i - 1]['x'], run['x'] - gap) out['production'] = actual # Tooling: a bar per tool mounted on the asset, in its colour, for its time on it in the range (custom.tooling: back to back # mounts of one tool are one). The hover has when it went on and off and how long text = lambda secs: system.kanoa.utilities.secondsToText(int(secs), {'showSecs': False, 'showDays': False}) or '' tools = [] for m in value['tooling'] or []: on = fmt(m['x']) if m['mountedInRange'] else 'before the range' lines = ['%s' % escape(m['name'] or ''), 'Mounted %s to %s (%s in this range)' % (on, fmt(m['x2']), text(m['secs']))] tools.append({'x': m['x'], 'x2': m['x2'], 'label': m['name'], 'color': m['color'], 'tip': '
'.join(lines)}) out['tooling'] = tools # Long ranges: the plot is about 1,500 pixels wide, so bars shorter than a pixel's worth of time can't be told apart. They're # drawn added up per pixel (thin, below), so a row has at most about 3,000 bars at any range: a year of a busy machine had # tens of thousands, enough to stop the browser. The Downtime and Speed Loss summaries still use every event (custom.timeline) values = value['values'] or {} try: w = (system.date.toMillis(values['endDate']) - system.date.toMillis(values['startDate'])) / 1500.0 except: w = 0 def thin(bars, what): # A bar at least a pixel wide stays as it is (they can't overlap, so there are at most about 1,500). Shorter ones are # added up per pixel-wide slot and drawn as one bar per slot, as wide as their time in it, so a slot that was 30% down # shows 30%; in the colour of the state with the most time there, its hover listing them if not bars or w <= 0: return bars t0 = system.date.toMillis(values['startDate']) keep, slots = [], {} for b in bars: if b['x2'] - b['x'] >= w: keep.append(b) continue k = int((b['x'] - t0) // w) slots.setdefault(k, []).append(b) for k in sorted(slots): grp = slots[k] if len(grp) == 1: keep.append(grp[0]) continue secs = {} for b in grp: secs[b.get('label')] = secs.get(b.get('label'), 0) + (b['x2'] - b['x']) / 1000.0 total = sum(secs.values()) top = max(secs, key=lambda n: secs[n]) first = [b for b in grp if b.get('label') == top][0] x = t0 + k * w lines = ['%d %s · %s' % (len(grp), what, text(total))] names = sorted(secs, key=lambda n: -secs[n]) for n in names[:5]: lines.append('%s: %s' % (escape(n or ''), text(secs[n]))) if len(names) > 5: lines.append('and %d more' % (len(names) - 5)) lines.append('%s to %s' % (fmt(min([b['x'] for b in grp])), fmt(max([b['x2'] for b in grp])))) keep.append(dict(first, x=x, x2=x + min(total * 1000.0, w), secs=total, tip='
'.join(lines))) keep.sort(key=lambda b: b['x']) return keep out['downtime'] = thin(out.get('downtime'), 'downtime events') out['performance'] = thin(out.get('performance'), 'speed loss events') return out

# The tools mounted directly on the asset over the chart's range, oldest first, each with a colour, for the timeline's
	# Tooling row. One getHistory by machine (868mvzzfr) gives everything mounted on it in the range
	values = value['values'] or {}
	start, end, assetId = values.get('startDate'), values.get('endDate'), values.get('assetId')
	if assetId is None or start is None or end is None: return []
	now = system.date.now()
	t0, t1 = system.date.toMillis(start), min(system.date.toMillis(end), system.date.toMillis(now))
	history = system.kanoa.tooling.getHistory({'assetId': assetId, 'start': start, 'end': end})
	mounts = []
	for row in system.dataset.toPyDataSet(history) if history is not None else []:
		# Only a tool on the asset itself; a tool in another tool's pocket moves with it
		if row['parentToolingAssetId'] is not None: continue
		s = max(system.date.toMillis(row['startDate']), t0)
		e = min(system.date.toMillis(row['endDate']) if row['endDate'] else t1, t1)
		if e <= s: continue
		mounts.append({'name': row['toolingName'], 'toolingAssetId': row['toolingAssetId'], 'x': s, 'x2': e, 'mountedInRange': system.date.toMillis(row['startDate']) >= t0})
	mounts.sort(key=lambda m: m['x'])
	# The same tool taken off and put back (often seconds apart) isn't a change: back-to-back mounts of one tool are one
	merged = []
	for m in mounts:
		if merged and merged[-1]['name'] == m['name']:
			merged[-1]['x2'] = max(merged[-1]['x2'], m['x2'])
			merged[-1]['secs'] += (m['x2'] - m['x']) / 1000
			continue
		m['secs'] = (m['x2'] - m['x']) / 1000
		merged.append(m)
	# A fixed palette, as the timeline's bars take a colour value, not a theme variable
	palette = ['#0069ad', '#f96900', '#f7b801', '#358a61', '#8a428c', '#489fe2', '#ba1a1a', '#5e1675']
	colors = {}
	for m in merged:
		if m['name'] not in colors: colors[m['name']] = palette[len(colors) % len(palette)]
		m['color'] = colors[m['name']]
	return merged

customMethods.script:
# Opens what a summary section links to, for the chart's asset and range (custom.links has the rights; a section links only
	# when the user can act there). One summary popup at a time: the last one (all open under one id) and the editors its
	# lists open close first, as a popup already open under an id isn't replaced by opening it again. Not modal: the chart
	# stays usable
	links = self.view.custom.links
	if not links or links.assetId is None or links.start is None: return
	now = system.date.now()
	# The editors that add or code events get the range's end at most now, as the Asset Operation info panel opens them
	endNow = links.end if links.end is not None and not system.date.isAfter(links.end, now) else now
	name = links.assetName or ''
	listValue = {'assetId': links.assetId, 'assetName': links.assetName, 'startDate': links.start, 'endDate': links.end, 'label': None,
		'match': [], 'targets': []}
	view, title, value = None, '', None
	if kind == 'scrap' and links.canEditOperations:
		# The Scrap editor: the range's waste entries by reason, grouped and coded in place (a group's entries keep to their own
		# time), and the runs' waste with no waste counts
		view, title = 'kanoa/mes/analytics/widgets/productionCounts/scrapEditor', 'Scrap - %s' % name
		value = {'assetId': links.assetId, 'assetName': links.assetName, 'assetPath': links.assetPath, 'startDate': links.start, 'endDate': endNow}
	elif kind == 'counts' and links.canEditOperations:
		# The count editor (as the info panel's Output chevron opens it), where waste is also coded with a reason
		view, title = 'kanoa/mes/asset/counts/countEditor', 'Count Editor - %s' % name
		value = {'assetId': links.assetId, 'assetPath': links.assetPath, 'startDate': links.start, 'endDate': endNow}
	elif kind == 'downtime' and links.canEditOperations:
		# The downtime table, as the Notifications widget opens it, with all the range's downtime (coded or not)
		view, title = 'kanoa/mes/asset/downtime/downtimeTable', 'Downtime - %s' % name
		value = {'assetId': links.assetId, 'assetPath': links.assetPath, 'startDate': links.start, 'endDate': endNow,
			'options': {'minDurationMins': 0, 'showAllStates': False, 'showChanged': -1, 'showDurationSecs': False, 'sortDateAsc': False}}
	elif kind == 'speedLoss' and links.canEditOperations:
		view, title = 'kanoa/mes/analytics/widgets/productionCounts/summaryEvents', 'Speed Loss - %s' % name
		value = dict(listValue, kind='speedLoss')
	elif kind == 'checks' and links.canEnterChecks:
		view, title = 'kanoa/mes/analytics/widgets/productionCounts/summaryEvents', 'Quality Checks - %s' % name
		value = dict(listValue, kind='checks')
	elif kind == 'workOrders' and links.canEditWorkOrders:
		# The work orders on the asset and on each tool mounted on it in the range, as custom.events reads them
		targets = [{'assetId': links.assetId, 'name': None}]
		for m in self.view.custom.tooling or []:
			if m['toolingAssetId'] and m['toolingAssetId'] not in [t['assetId'] for t in targets]: targets.append({'assetId': m['toolingAssetId'], 'name': m['name']})
		view, title = 'kanoa/mes/analytics/widgets/productionCounts/summaryEvents', 'Maintenance - %s' % name
		value = dict(listValue, kind='workOrders', targets=targets)
	elif kind == 'spc':
		# The Measure SPC Analysis (as the Notifications widget opens a measure's alert) over the range: of the measure with the
		# most serious alerts, the first listed on a tie
		measures = [m for m in (self.view.custom.spcAlerts or {}).get('measures') or [] if m['tagPath']]
		if not measures: return
		rank = lambda m: (m['limit'], m['pattern'], m['variation'])
		best = measures[0]
		for m in measures[1:]:
			if rank(m) > rank(best): best = m
		view, title = 'kanoa/core/dbp/widgets/analytics/measureSPCAnalysis', 'Measure SPC Analysis'
		value = {'tagPath': best['tagPath'], 'startDate': links.start, 'endDate': links.end}
	if view is None: return
	for popupId in ('productionSummary', 'speedLossReason', 'productionSummaryCheck', 'productionSummaryWorkOrder'): system.perspective.closePopup(popupId)
	system.perspective.openPopup('productionSummary', view, {'value': value}, title=title, draggable=True, resizable=True, showCloseIcon=True,
		viewportBound=True)
	return
